card.name: The word You starting a sentence
card.fires_on: The word "You" (or "thou") as the first word of a new sentence or reply, addressing the reader directly. Often follows a thank-you, a statement of advice, or a side-effect reporting line.

modes.label: Reply after thanks
modes.description: "You" opens a polite response such as "You're welcome" in a dialogue or comment reply.
modes.example: Host: Dr. Piwnica-Worms, thank you for joining us. Piwnica-Worms:<< You>>’re welcome.

modes.label: Label advice sentence
modes.description: "You" begins a sentence telling the reader what they may do, such as ask a provider or report side effects.
modes.example: Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.<< You>> may report side effects to FDA at

modes.label: Direct address in web text
modes.description: "You" or "thou" starts a sentence in forum, site or older prose addressing the reader or another person.
modes.example: Join our mailing list to receive updates on new content on Library, our latest ebooks, and more. <<You>> won't be inundated with emails!

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning "know" and "knowing", as in "you know", including Chinese forms.
card.plain: It fires when a sentence starts with "You" and speaks straight to the reader.
